rubrics.name: complete_cohort_population_reconciled
rubrics.rubric: The outputs carry the complete July cohort through the readiness package.
criterion: All ten Rep_IDs REP-2701 through REP-2710 are present in the playbook appendix, schedule workbook, certification register, and coverage model.
Representative names, supervisors, segments, target certification dates, and target independent coverage dates match the July intake evidence.
No representative is dropped because they are blocked, pending, or not yet ready.

rubrics.name: competency_requirements_applied
rubrics.rubric: The certification evidence is checked against the governed competency standard.
criterion: The register applies all seven competencies GS-C01 through GS-C07 to every representative, for 70 representative-competency rows.
Minimum rules are applied consistently: GS-C01 85, GS-C02 88, GS-C03 90, GS-C05 95, GS-C06 85, GS-C07 90 plus signoff, and GS-C04 pass with no critical miss.
Assessment, observation, CRM, coaching, and exception evidence are traceable to the supplied exports rather than summarized without row-level references.

rubrics.name: readiness_dispositions_correct
rubrics.rubric: The package derives the current readiness mix correctly.
criterion: The readiness summary shows exactly 3 ready-pending-manager representatives: REP-2701, REP-2707, and REP-2710.
It shows exactly 1 approved limited-exception representative, REP-2702, and does not treat that exception as full independent coverage approval.
It shows REP-2703 and REP-2705 as remediation required, REP-2706 and REP-2709 as pending evidence, and REP-2704 and REP-2708 as blocked by unresolved exception.

rubrics.name: pending_approval_state_preserved
rubrics.rubric: The outputs remain an approval-ready request, not an execution notice.
criterion: The playbook and all workbooks identify HB-RAMP-2026-07 as pending desk manager approval.
No output states that independent customer coverage has already been approved for any representative.
Rows with existing evidence approval, such as REP-2702's limited exception, remain distinguishable from rows that only have staged or proposed actions.

rubrics.name: limited_exception_handled_correctly
rubrics.rubric: The approved limited exception is used only within its evidence boundary.
criterion: REP-2702 is allowed only for staged supervised low-risk affinity coverage until the 2026-07-20 live observation closes.
The coverage model does not allocate high-risk or independent coverage to REP-2702.
The register and playbook retain the GS-C07 evidence gap and the EX-LIM-2702 approval note together.

rubrics.name: schedule_remaining_work_feasible
rubrics.rubric: The training and observation schedule resolves remaining work without violating visible constraints.
criterion: The schedule includes Priya's CRM remediation and retest on 2026-07-16, Sofia's contract remediation on 2026-07-16 and retest on 2026-07-17, Liam's live observation on 2026-07-17, Isabella's supervisor panel on 2026-07-17, and Jordan's live observation on 2026-07-20. It also carries Noah's compliance remediation and retest path without hiding whether the visible constraints allow a compliant slot.
Scheduled events respect trainer qualifications, visible availability windows, and stated buffer rules.
No scheduled trainer-date booking exceeds the supplied capacity slots.

rubrics.name: schedule_blackouts_and_exclusions_respected
rubrics.rubric: The schedule preserves blocked and unavailable states rather than forcing them into infeasible slots.
criterion: No live observation is scheduled with TRN-505 during the 2026-07-17 13:00-17:00 QA calibration blackout.
No compliance event is scheduled with TRN-504 on 2026-07-20 during the privacy audit blackout.
REP-2704 remains unscheduled for certification closure until the licensing hold is cleared, with compliance as owner and 2026-07-22 as due date.

rubrics.name: register_exceptions_complete
rubrics.rubric: The certification register preserves every material exception and next action.
criterion: The exception view includes EX-LIM-2702, EX-REM-2703, EX-LIC-2704, EX-CRM-2705, EX-LIVE-2706, EX-COMP-2708, and EX-PANEL-2709.
Each exception has a reason, approval state, owner, next action, opened date, and due date.
Unresolved exceptions for REP-2704 and REP-2708 are not converted into ready, scheduled-ready, or handoff-ready statuses.

rubrics.name: coverage_allocation_counts_correct
rubrics.rubric: The coverage model produces the correct staged disposition for every active account.
criterion: Across 16 active accounts, the model shows 5 staged eligible handoffs, 2 staged limited supervised assignments, 6 remaining under temporary coverage, and 3 escalations to supervisors.
Every Account_ID ACC-1001 through ACC-1016 has exactly one coverage disposition.
The allocation statuses are formula-driven or otherwise traceable to readiness status and risk band evidence.

rubrics.name: coverage_dependency_blocks_unready_reps
rubrics.rubric: Account handoffs obey readiness and exception dependencies.
criterion: Accounts proposed for REP-2703, REP-2705, REP-2706, and REP-2709 remain under temporary coverage while remediation or pending evidence remains open.
Accounts proposed for REP-2704 and REP-2708 are escalated because of unresolved licensing or compliance blockers.
No account is staged as an independent eligible handoff to a representative who is remediation-required, pending evidence, or blocked.

rubrics.name: account_continuity_preserved
rubrics.rubric: The coverage plan protects customer commitments during pending approval.
criterion: Every account row carries the current temporary owner, proposed rep, service deadline, customer action due, risk band, quoted value, and margin estimate.
High-risk or deadline-sensitive accounts ACC-1004, ACC-1010, and ACC-1013 have named supervisor escalation ownership and next actions.
Owner load analysis flags that SUP-410 retains 4 accounts against a capacity limit of 3 after staged handoffs.

rubrics.name: coverage_financial_totals_reconcile
rubrics.rubric: The model reconciles quoted value and margin exposure from the account source.
criterion: Total quoted value across the account population reconciles to USD 1,942,000.
Quoted value remaining in temporary coverage plus supervisor escalation after applying the limited-exception scenario reconciles to USD 1,346,000.

Financial exposure is traceable to row-level account dispositions and clearly distinguishes value proposed for staged handoff from value retained under temporary coverage or supervisor escalation rather than presenting one unexplained hardcoded total.

rubrics.name: playbook_operating_logic_complete
rubrics.rubric: The playbook gives supervisors a usable governed workflow.
criterion: The playbook includes entry criteria, RACI ownership, decision points, exception routes, escalation paths, and staged handoff checklist fields.
Its process-flow diagram reflects intake, curriculum, supervised practice, evidence review, remediation, approved limited exception, temporary coverage continuation, and pending manager handoff.

The representative-specific appendix carries every representative's readiness status and next action, while open-evidence ownership, due dates, and coverage restrictions are available in the playbook's exception and control sections or the linked companion deliverables.

rubrics.name: cross_deliverable_status_consistency
rubrics.rubric: The four deliverables use the same status and date facts.
criterion: Readiness statuses in the playbook appendix match the certification register and the coverage model.
Schedule dates for remaining evidence items match the next actions and due dates in the register.
Coverage restrictions in the playbook match allocation statuses in the coverage model.

rubrics.name: formula_and_check_lineage_present
rubrics.rubric: Decision-critical calculations are supported by workbook formulas and check sheets.
criterion: The schedule workbook uses formulas for duration, capacity, booked slots, conflict flags, and schedule control totals.
The certification register uses formulas for complete counts, evidence percentages, readiness status, and cohort reconciliation checks.
The coverage model uses formulas for readiness lookup, handoff eligibility, allocation status, risk score, staged-versus-retained value totals, and account control checks.

rubrics.name: professional_style_docx_native_rendering
rubrics.rubric: The Word playbook is a readable native DOCX.
criterion: The DOCX opens and renders without blank pages, clipped text, broken glyphs, or overlapping content.
It uses semantic headings, an automatic contents element, headers or footers, and native editable tables rather than screenshots of text.
Document properties contain realistic HarborBridge title, subject, authoring role, and operational keywords.

rubrics.name: professional_style_docx_tables_and_diagrams
rubrics.rubric: The Word tables and process diagram are usable in rendered and native form.
criterion: RACI, decision, appendix, and checklist tables have readable column widths, high-contrast repeated headers, and row-level content that does not spill outside cells.
The process-flow diagram is embedded in the DOCX as an editable table or Office object with clear lanes and exception branches.
Captions or source notes keep the diagram tied to the evidence instead of floating as decoration.

rubrics.name: professional_style_schedule_xlsx_native_execution
rubrics.rubric: The schedule workbook behaves like a native scheduling packet.
criterion: Date, time, duration, capacity, and status fields use native Excel data types and formats rather than display-only text.
Tables have filters, frozen headings, validation lists where useful, conditional formatting for conflicts or risk, and no visible formula errors.

The opening control or summary view makes schedule feasibility, conflicts, exclusions, owners, and due dates reviewable from live row-level records. Charts are optional and, when used, are tied to live worksheet ranges.

rubrics.name: professional_style_register_xlsx_native_execution
rubrics.rubric: The certification register is a controlled workbook.
criterion: The register exposes row-level representative-competency records with stable IDs, filters, frozen panes, validation lists, and controlled status fields.
Summary and check sheets remain visible, readable, and free of formula errors.
Readiness, gaps, exception aging, and evidence completeness are summarized from live row-level data. Charts are optional and, when used, use live ranges.

rubrics.name: professional_style_coverage_xlsx_native_execution
rubrics.rubric: The coverage model is organized as a native analytical workbook.
criterion: The workbook separates source records, allocation logic, capacity and priority analysis, checks, and decision summaries clearly enough to trace each disposition back to its inputs.
Currency, percentages, dates, and counts use native numeric formats and readable precision.
Allocation, value-at-risk, deadlines, capacity, and risk are summarized from visible live ranges. Charts are optional and, when used, remain bound to those ranges.

rubrics.name: professional_style_visuals_are_evidence_based
rubrics.rubric: The required visuals clarify the operational decision.
criterion: The required DOCX process diagram and workbook control or summary views each answer a specific readiness, scheduling, exception, or coverage question.
Any charts have readable titles, axes or legends, units or counts, and no redundant decorative duplicates.
Visuals do not introduce unsupported categories or values absent from the source room.

rubrics.name: professional_style_template_and_metadata_scrubbed
rubrics.rubric: The package contains no builder or template residue.
criterion: Visible text and native metadata use business-facing HarborBridge language and do not expose irrelevant implementation or generation details.
No unused sample sheets, sample ranges, placeholder text, comments, or hidden template content remains in the deliverables.
The four output files use consistent HarborBridge naming, dates, pending-state language, and document control details.
